sections.value:
PASS-WITH-NOTES - reviewer/294, F240, round 1
Head: 7704c7ec932c514de975442ca1ae03d62abc6300
Base: 0587a416611096daa0712e96fe161f47b81e87d2

No blocking findings. Read-only review of all three changed files; no source
changes or reviewer mutations.

Ownership (crates/tmux/src/control.rs:331-358): the first bounded poll owns the
Child exclusively. After it expires, the Child lives in one Option slot.
The reaper's and_then closure takes it and drops the MutexGuard before wait().
On successful spawn the caller never takes it; on a failed production spawn
the reaper closure never runs, and dropping its Arc leaves the caller's Arc
and Child intact. Taking the Option is exclusive. The new Mutex cannot be
poisoned by a failed child.wait(), which executes outside the guard.

Normal handoff: same named detached thread and blocking child.wait(), with no
caller join or second poll after successful spawn. The existing real-thread
handoff test and the real tmux drop/release integration tests pass.

Bounds (control.rs:232-243, 331-374): Done returns after the first bounded poll;
Handed returns after that poll and a successful thread start; only Err adds a
second REAP_WAIT. Left returns the owned Child and logs its numeric pid.
The configured client-exit budget is TEARDOWN_WAIT + 2 * REAP_WAIT = 3 s on
spawn failure, versus 2 s otherwise. These are configured waits, with normal
poll/scheduler overhead, not hard real-time guarantees. The docs describe the extra second, but their literal whole-exit ceiling needs
the qualification below. F242 runs release concurrently with HTTP/workers
(crates/daemon/src/lib.rs:353-410); its 5 s HTTP drain is not a global daemon
stop deadline, and later admitted-write/pool cleanup has a separate deadline.

C34 follow-up P294-OBS1 (corroborated, non-blocking): qualify "whole exit at most 3 s" as
the configured wait sum. The new Left warning at control.rs:298-303 writes
synchronously to stderr, outside those waits. Performance/294 traced the
daemon's stderr through a blocking UnixStream and a synchronous original-sink
copier; backpressure can therefore hold that warning without an independent
deadline. The new tests exercise reap_with, not reap's warning. No new
normal-use hang was observed or claimed; this is a bound qualification, not
a demand for new logging machinery. Performance published the same note as
P294-OBS1 in governance commit ff25bacb5749fb6f15755df87ef33234e0ce73c2.

Privacy: the only new log formats child.id(), with fixed text, no argv,
environment, secret, or machine-local path. No launch site is added.

Cost: no steady-state change. The existing slow-handoff branch adds an Arc,
Mutex and boxed closure, once per delayed client exit; the successful path
still starts one reaper thread. Spawn failure adds roughly 200 non-blocking
try_wait polls at 5 ms intervals for at most one configured second, with no
new process or thread. Live cost collection belongs to performance/294.

Evidence:
- just pr-freeze 294: FINAL at the exact head; CLEAN, all latest checks pass.
- PIJ_SHARED_TARGET="$(bash harness/scripts/cargo-target.sh)" just shared-build
  -- fmt --all -- --check --then clippy -p pij-tmux --all-targets --
  -D warnings --then test -p pij-tmux: exit 0 on macOS, nice 19, locked,
  four jobs/test threads. 110 tests passed: 40 lib (2.05 s), 41 adapter
  (58.46 s), 23 control_mode (6.46 s), 6 control_teardown (0.29 s).
  Both new no-reaper tests and the existing real-thread handoff test passed.
- git diff --check 0587a416..HEAD: exit 0; review worktree remains clean.
- CI run 44761679040: success at this full head; Rust lint/test and both
  Node 22/24 checks passed. Delivers run 44761678730 also passed.
- harness checks: exit 1, NOT a green local ship gate. Rust workspace
  fmt/clippy/tests, route inventory, pij skill and Copilot native contracts
  passed. TS/path/docs/coverage/lockfile tools failed without pinned local
  dependencies (tsx/vitest absent); ambient Biome rejected the v2 config.
  Smoke exited 143: I stopped only my shared-build waiter after it waited
  behind the occupied target lock, leaving that holder untouched. No full
  local smoke claim. No dependencies were installed or linked. Node 22/24
  typecheck, lint and tests are instead proved by the exact-head CI run.

Accepted residual: after both bounded waits, a client still not waitable when
no reaper thread can start is explicitly left unreaped. This is disclosed,
not a silent success, and keeps the reaping waits bounded. C34 applies;
the author's mutation descriptions in the PR body were not repeated or
independently attested.

Harness feedback:
magicWand: a read-only review gate profile that reports TS proof as CI-only
under C25 and accepts exact-head CI receipts, rather than recommending
dependency repair that the review contract forbids.
difficulties: boot returned NOT-READY for absent vitest and suggested
worktree-deps; C25 and this packet require leaving dependencies untouched.
The full gate nevertheless ran unavailable TS tooling and a broad Rust gate,
then waited behind the shared build lock for smoke; its per-stage result was
not visible until the final envelope. A review profile should surface that
CI-only proof disposition and stage progress instead of requiring inference.
No product-tree retro or ledger edits were made in this read-only worktree.
Keep the reviewer/294 holding until merge.
